properties.endpoint: Today: inherent methods on `reflow2_core::DesignGraph` (crates/reflow2-core/src/graph.rs). After extraction: a `reflow2_core::GraphRead` trait, taken as `&dyn GraphRead` — the shape `LlmBackend` already uses in 6 call sites and the only proven swap point in the crate.
properties.error_model:
`Result<T, DynoError>`, where DynoError is dynograph-foundation's error type — inherited with the payload types, not defined here.

ABSENCE IS NOT AN ERROR, and this is the load-bearing clause for anyone writing a second implementation:
  — a node that does not exist is `Ok(None)`, never `Err`
  — a type with no nodes, or a node with no matching edges, is `Ok(vec![])`, never `Err`
  — an UNKNOWN node_type is a real error and must NOT be answered `Ok(None)` or `Ok(vec![])`. "No such type" and "no such node" are different facts and must not share a reply — `get_node` already refuses this way at the tool surface, and an implementation that collapsed them would silently answer "nothing there" for every typo.

An `Err` therefore means the store could not answer, never that the answer was empty. A conforming implementation that returned empty on failure would satisfy the signatures and break every caller's meaning, which is why this is written down rather than left to the types.
properties.name: Graph read API — the five operations a module needs to read a design without being able to change it
properties.operations:
FIVE OPERATIONS, ALL `&self`, ALL READ-ONLY. Derived by counting every call site in reflow2-core, not chosen by taste — these five carry 324 of the calls that reach the store.

  fn get_node(&self, node_type: &str, id: &str) -> Result<Option<StoredNode>, DynoError>
  fn scan_nodes(&self, node_type: &str) -> Result<Vec<StoredNode>, DynoError>
  fn count_nodes(&self, node_type: &str) -> Result<usize, DynoError>
  fn outgoing(&self, from_id: &str, edge_type: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<StoredEdge>, DynoError>
  fn incoming(&self, to_id: &str, edge_type: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<StoredEdge>, DynoError>

Call counts as measured 2026-08-21: get_node 113, scan_nodes 78, outgoing 59, incoming 57, count_nodes 17.

DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, and each exclusion is the contract saying something:
  — every write (create_edge 55, upsert_node 22, delete_node 3, delete_edge 3). A module holding this contract CANNOT change the design, which is what makes a read-only module safe to swap and cheap to test.
  — `design_network` and the other derived views. They are BUILT from these five (structure.rs `build_network`), so they are consumers of this contract, not part of it. Putting a derived view in the contract would force every alternative implementation to reimplement reflow2's own analysis.
  — `engine()` and `graph_id()`. `search.rs` reaches through them to the storage engine directly, which is why search is NOT a clean consumer of this boundary despite calling only three methods. Naming that here is the point: the exclusion is what tells you search needs work before it can be swapped.
